transcript: 00:00 Alex (AE): okay starting now, thanks everyone for taking time, uh this is Alex from Redwood, i'll do a quick intro. 00:06 Priya (Customer): hi all, Priya here, ML eng, we're focused on a recommender microservice that streams partial context and needs low tail latency. 00:14 Samir (SE): great, Samir from Redwood infra — we'll pair on the harness wiring and the benchmark run. quick calibration — what's your current qps and tokens per request? 00:23 Marcus (Customer): today in prod we're at ~120 qps steady for inference, but spikes to 400 qps during batch windows, tokens average about 60 per request, some longer sessions 300+. 00:35 Hannah (Product): our user-facing SLO is p95 under 200ms right now, but the ML team wants to aim for p95 120ms for the POC to validate UX. 00:47 Alex: okay p95 120ms — good to capture as a target. for the harness, do you plan to stream partial responses to clients or only return completed generations? 00:56 Priya: we stream; the real product sends partial tokens as they arrive — latency matters per token. think realtime. 01:04 Samir: that's important — streaming changes harness behavior a bit — we'll need to verify streaming path through our runtime and how the customer adapter sends events. 01:13 Priya: our current client has a socket that forwards tokens, but the offline test scripts we've got are batch-style. that's the mismatch. 01:22 Alex: perfect, so we should get your live-style script. Priya, can you share one of those socket adapters or a small simulator? 01:28 Priya: yes, i'll share a trimmed script. 01:31 Marcus: also want to mention security — we run in a locked VPC, so peering and egress are a thing. do you support KMS integration for key wrap? 01:39 Jordan (Solutions Eng): yes we do — Redwood Private supports customer KMS and we can surface a short doc. we'll also produce SOC2 artifacts on request. 01:47 Marcus: okay good. 01:49 Alex: on the harness side, we support two modes: streaming-mode where the harness emits token-level delta and measures per-token latency, and batch-mode which waits for full completions and measures completion latency. each has different throughput behaviors and cost profiles. 02:03 Priya: can you explain the tradeoffs briefly? 02:06 Samir: sure — streaming-mode gives you realistic tail latency for interactive clients and allows measuring first-byte time and p95 token latency; batch-mode is easier to scale for sustained throughput and can amortize KV cache hits better. streaming tends to lower throughput because of more RPCs and smaller payloads. 02:26 Hannah: our acceptance criteria should include both: p95 per-token <120ms for streaming small prompts, and average tokens/sec throughput >= X for batch runs. we don't yet have an exact throughput number. 02:38 Alex: let's capture a workload matrix — small prompt (avg 60 tokens) targeted p95 120ms at 300 qps; long session (avg 300 tokens) targeted completion p95 500ms at 80 concurrent sessions. does that align? 02:50 Marcus: yes that approximates our peak patterns. 02:54 Priya: one nuance — we leverage kv cache between messages in a session; the harness must simulate warm sessions and cold sessions separately. 03:03 Samir: good call — we'll define warm vs cold percentages in the harness config. typical split we recommend: 70% warm, 30% cold for your workload but we can tune. 03:14 Alex: on observability — we will capture tokenized latency, first-byte, completion time, GPU utilization, and per-request memory delta. are there any custom telemetry points you need? 03:24 Priya: please capture a session-id so we can map to our client traces; also include a correlation id header we use. 03:31 Jordan: we'll add that header to the harness request template. 03:35 Marcus: about cost — if we run streaming mode for the whole POC it might be expensive. any suggestions to limit cost while still validating latency? 03:44 Samir: run a mixed-mode: targeted streaming runs for tail-latency validation on a representative sample, plus larger-scale batch runs to verify throughput and cost curves. also use prefix caching for repeated prompts to simulate warm sessions. 03:57 Priya: how do we handle tokenization differences between our tokenizer and the model? we've had small mismatches before causing token counts to differ. 04:06 Alex: include a preflight step in the harness to run tokenizer validation: feed sample prompts and compare token counts and token boundaries — we can add a mapping script. 04:15 Priya: great. 04:18 Hannah: timeline — we want a baseline run within two weeks. 04:22 Alex: doable. Samir, can you provide a 2-hour lab slot next Tue? 04:27 Samir: yes i'll propose two windows and include preflight checklist — expecting Phil from infra for network whitelisting. 04:36 Marcus: one more — for security signoff, we need an exportable audit log and confirmation we can restrict retention. is that supported? 04:45 Jordan: yes logs are configurable and we support retention policies, plus we can demonstrate KMS encryption at rest for artifact store. 04:53 Priya: perfect. 04:55 Alex: wrapping up — recap: we need customer's streaming adapter script, sample prompts, target workload matrix, Redwood sends harness + quickstart, schedule lab, and run mixed streaming + batch tests. 05:05 Hannah: sounds good. 05:07 Alex: any blockers? 05:08 Priya: none immediate — i'll share scripts by tomorrow. 05:11 Marcus: i'll confirm network window by EOD Friday. 05:16 Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the repo link. 05:20 (call ends)\n\nNotes on transcript quality: occasional speaker ID glitch at ~01:31 where "Vendor: John" is labeled as customer, minor mis-transcriptions (kv cache -> k v cache), and some run-ons.
